What are the four IMCI general danger signs?
Unable to drink or breastfeed, vomits everything, convulsions, and lethargy or unconsciousness.
What is done for a child with IMCI very severe febrile disease?
Give the first dose of antibiotic and of antimalarial, treat low blood glucose, and refer urgently.
Which fever is a red flag in young infants?
Any fever of 38 °C or more under 3 months of age.

Which test is done for every febrile child in a malaria area?
A malaria rapid diagnostic test or a blood film.
How is a febrile baby under 1 month of age managed?
Admission, a full septic screen (blood, urine and lumbar puncture) and intravenous antibiotics.

Is tepid sponging recommended for fever?
No. Light clothing and fluids are used instead.
How is fever of unknown origin defined?
A fever of 38 °C or more on most days for more than 2–3 weeks, with no cause found after 1 week of investigation.
What are the infectious causes of prolonged fever in Sudan?
Typhoid, brucellosis, tuberculosis, kala-azar, malaria, urinary tract infection, endocarditis and HIV infection.
What are the non-infectious causes of prolonged fever?
Kawasaki disease, systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, rheumatic fever, systemic lupus erythematosus, leukaemia and lymphoma.
What are the features of Kawasaki disease?
Fever for 5 days or more, with red eyes, red cracked lips, a rash, swollen hands and feet, and an enlarged neck node.
A child has fever, hepatosplenomegaly and pancytopenia. What should be considered?
Kala-azar; leukaemia is the other important cause.
